implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control (P06) was approved 2026-09-22, replacing the 2024 version. The authenticator and privileged access standard (STD-06) and the account review procedure are due 2026-12-31.

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); ATS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Internal staff accounts are created in the identity provider from HR tickets and federated to the ATS, payroll platform, credentialing platform, cloud accounts, and productivity suite. Associate self-service accounts are created by the ATS at onboarding. Gaps: SSO access reviews are semi-annual (last March 2026); ATS roles, E-Verify, the VMS, and credentialing client users are never reviewed; E-Verify and VMS accounts are managed by hand outside SSO (EV-004, EV-006; P07 found 3 E-Verify and 4 VMS accounts of departed staff, EV-AC-2).
evidence: EV-001 (IdP export); EV-006 (ATS role matrix); EV-010 and EV-011 (E-Verify and VMS user lists); EV-AC-2 (termination sample of 25)
regulatory_driver: N56-BM (PR.AA-01); E-Verify MOU Art. II.A.3; N56-R03 (8 CFR 274a.2(g)(1)(i))

implementation_statement: Account creation, disablement, and removal for SSO applications are automated from the HR ticket workflow in the identity provider.
The identity provider disables staff accounts after 45 days without sign-in. Gap: local accounts in E-Verify, the VMS, and the credentialing client portal are not covered.
evidence: EV-002 (IdP inactivity policy); EV-010, EV-011 and EV-012 (local account lists)

provider_if_inherited: ATS vendor; payroll vendor; credentialing vendor
implementation_statement: The ATS enforces 31 custom roles and branch assignment; the payroll platform separates payroll, billing, and administrator roles. Gaps: 262 users in recruiter, branch manager, and account manager roles can open I-9 document images and consumer reports for all branches; credential files with medical information are visible to all 30 Healthcare recruiters (EV-006, EV-012).
evidence: EV-006 (ATS role matrix); EV-012 (credentialing role export); EV-AC-3 (P07 test account results)

implementation_statement: The cloud hub firewall restricts flows between the shared services and workloads accounts; the integration platform reaches SaaS APIs only through the egress proxy. Gap: lobby kiosks share the staff network at 9 of 14 branches.
evidence: EV-016 (firewall rule export; SD-WAN segment report)

implementation_statement: The Controller approves each weekly payroll register and funding request; staff-requested bank changes need a call-back. Gaps: associate-entered bank changes take effect on the next payroll with no hold or second check (EV-007, EV-008); 2 payroll specialists can both add an associate and change pay rates.
evidence: EV-008 (payroll approval log; payroll role export)

implementation_statement: Staff have no local administrator rights on laptops. Gaps: 46 users can query the data warehouse, which holds full SSNs and bank account numbers (EV-024); the 2 backup administrators also hold workload administrator rights.
evidence: EV-024 (warehouse user list); EV-021 (cloud role export)

implementation_statement: IT staff have separate administrator accounts for the identity provider and cloud consoles. Gap: ATS and payroll platform administrators use their everyday accounts.
Cloud administrator roles are limited to 4 named IT staff and require just-in-time elevation. Gap: 3 ATS administrators and 2 payroll administrators have standing rights with no periodic review.
evidence: EV-021 (cloud role assignments); EV-005 (SaaS admin lists)

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts; the associate portal locks after 5 failed attempts.
Laptops lock after 10 minutes idle through device management. Gap: kiosks run a shared local account and do not reset between applicants at 6 branches.

provider_if_inherited: ATS vendor; payroll vendor; credentialing vendor
implementation_statement: SaaS sessions end after 30 minutes idle (ATS, credentialing) and 20 minutes (payroll), as confirmed in vendor settings.
evidence: EV-007, EV-008 and EV-012 (SaaS security settings)

implementation_statement: Staff reach SaaS over TLS through SSO; on-site office laptops use an always-on VPN. The MSSP uses its EDR console with named accounts. Gap: the 3 contractor developers reach the code repository and the workloads account from unmanaged laptops.
evidence: EV-016 (remote access configuration); EV-028 (contractor access list)

implementation_statement: Staff Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication; guest Wi-Fi is isolated at every office.
The 230 company smartphones are enrolled in device management with passcode, encryption, and remote wipe.
On-site office laptops connect through client guest networks with the always-on VPN. Gap: no written terms with the 6 on-site clients for use of their networks.
Awareness and training requirements are in POL-05 (P06), approved 2026-09-22.
All internal staff complete annual awareness training (96% completion) and quarterly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 9.4%).
Phishing simulations include fake sign-in pages. Gap: no training on push-approval relay, caller impersonation for bank changes, or invoice redirection for payroll, billing, and MSP staff.

Every E-Verify user completed the E-Verify Tutorial (MOU Art. II.A.5). Gaps: no role training for payroll staff on bank-change fraud, for recruiters on FCRA and I-9 record limits, or for credentialing staff on ADA medical file rules.
regulatory_driver: E-Verify MOU Art. II.A.5; N56-R03 (8 CFR 274a.2(g)(1)(iii))

implementation_statement: Logging requirements are stated in POL-03; the logging and monitoring standard (STD-02) is due 2027-01-31.

provider_if_inherited: ATS vendor; payroll vendor; identity provider vendor; cloud provider
implementation_statement: The identity provider, email, EDR, firewalls, SD-WAN, and cloud control plane send logs to the SIEM. Gaps: ATS, payroll, VMS, and credentialing audit events are not sent (EV-026); object-level logging is off on the document archive.
evidence: EV-026 (SIEM source list); EV-025 (storage logging settings)

implementation_statement: ATS and payroll audit records include user, record, field, old and new value, time, and source address; the I-9 module keeps a per-form change history.
evidence: EV-031 (ATS I-9 audit history sample); EV-008 (payroll change report)

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews SIEM alerts 24x7. Gap: no review of payroll exports, bank-change volumes, ATS bulk downloads, or credentialing access, because those logs are not in the SIEM.
Planned: automated alert rules for payroll register exports, more than 20 bank changes in an hour, and ATS bulk document downloads, once the SaaS logs reach the SIEM (2027-01-31).
Cloud audit logs land in a write-once bucket in the security account. Gap: SaaS audit logs can be read and exported by SaaS administrators and are not copied to protected storage.
The SIEM keeps 1 year searchable; the cloud log bucket keeps 3 years. Gap: payroll platform audit reports are kept 180 days by the vendor and are not exported.
Audit generation is on by default in the SaaS systems and the cloud control plane. Gap: data access events are not generated for the document archive or the data warehouse.
The co-sourced internal audit firm assessed 35 controls from 2026-08-17 to 2026-09-04 (P07) and reports to the audit committee.

Interfaces with the payroll vendor, screening provider, and VMS vendor are covered by contracts. Gap: the integration platform connections to the timekeeping and credentialing vendors have no written interconnection terms.
Weaknesses are tracked in the P07 POA&M with owners and dates and reported to the audit committee each quarter.
The COO accepted operation of the APATP on 2026-09-22 with the conditions in section 4.2.
The MSSP runs continuous EDR and SIEM monitoring; the GRC analyst tracks POA&M status monthly. Gap: no metrics for SaaS configuration drift or vendor posture.
Configuration management requirements are in POL-01; the configuration standard (STD-01) is due 2027-03-31.
Gold images exist for laptops and kiosks; cloud guardrails define the landing zone baseline. Gap: no documented baseline for ATS, payroll, and credentialing tenant settings.

Infrastructure changes go through the IT ticket workflow with approval. Gap: changes to ATS workflows, payroll settings, and AI tool settings are made by administrators without review; the AI auto-advance setting was enabled in 2025-09 without approval (EV-020).
Device management enforces laptop settings; cloud guardrails deny public storage and unencrypted volumes. Gap: container and kiosk hardening are not documented.
Laptop images remove unneeded services. Gap: kiosks allow USB storage at the 9 unsegmented branches.

Laptops, smartphones, and kiosks are in device management. Gaps: the 12 fingerprint clocks, network devices at on-site offices, and the data stores that hold SSNs, I-9 images, and medical information are not inventoried.
Users cannot install software; requests go through the service desk.
Planned data inventory: where SSNs, I-9 images, consumer reports, medical information, biometric templates, and call recordings are stored. Today it covers the ATS and payroll platform only.
Contingency requirements are in POL-03; the contingency and recovery standard (STD-07) is due 2026-12-31.

The BIA (P05) was approved 2026-09-22. Gaps: no approved contingency plan, no off-cycle manual payroll procedure, and vendor recovery objectives were not compared with the BIA until 2026 (EV-036, EV-022). Plan due 2026-12-31.
The plan will be coordinated with the payroll vendor, the ATS vendor, and the credit line lender. Today only the hurricane plan for branches exists.
Planned: annual contingency training for payroll, credentialing, and branch staff after the plan is approved.

The data warehouse restore was tested 2026-03. Gaps: the document archive has never been restored; an integration platform restore attempted during P07 testing failed because its secrets were outside the backup scope; no payroll outage exercise has been held.
Backups are stored in a separate backup account in a second region.
SaaS vendors run their own alternate processing (payroll RTO 8 hours, ATS RTO 12 hours). Gap: the integration platform has no alternate region deployment.
HQ has dual ISPs. Gap: branches and on-site offices have a single circuit with LTE backup at 5 branches only.

provider_if_inherited: ATS vendor; payroll vendor; cloud provider
implementation_statement: SaaS data is backed up by the vendors. The data warehouse and integration platform are backed up daily to the backup account with 30-day write-once retention. Gap: the document archive is replicated, not backed up (EV-036, EV-022).
Backup jobs report success daily. Gap: integrity is not tested by restore except for the warehouse.
Workloads can be rebuilt from infrastructure templates in the landing zone. Gap: recovery procedures and order are not documented; the BIA order (P05) will be used.
Identification and authentication requirements are in POL-02.

Staff authenticate with unique IDs through the identity provider. Associates use the ATS associate portal and mobile app with the vendor login and SMS one-time codes, which do not resist SIM swap or credential stuffing (EV-007, EV-008). E-Verify and VMS use separate local accounts.
evidence: EV-001 (IdP user export); EV-007 (ATS associate login settings)

implementation_statement: Number-matching push MFA is required for all administrator accounts under SSO, including cloud, ATS, and payroll administrators.
All staff have number-matching push MFA through SSO; VMS users have app-based codes. Gap: associates use SMS codes (EV-007, EV-008).

Number matching and one-time codes resist simple replay. Gap: push approvals can still be relayed by adversary-in-the-middle phishing; phishing-resistant authenticators for payroll and administrators are planned for 2027-03-31.

The identity provider enforces a 14-character minimum and a banned-password list. Gaps: kiosks share one local password; a payroll platform API key with write access to bank-account fields was stored in plain text in the integration container image and repository (found in P07, EV-IA-5).
evidence: EV-002 (IdP password policy); EV-IA-5 (P07 IA-5 results)

provider_if_inherited: ATS vendor; credentialing vendor; VMS vendor
implementation_statement: Client supervisors, hospital compliance staff, and MSP supplier users sign in to the client portal, credentialing client portal, and VMS with vendor-managed accounts. Gap: client users in the credentialing portal have no MFA and are never reviewed.

New associates are identity-proofed at hire through Form I-9 document examination (in person at branches or the DHS remote alternative procedure) and E-Verify before an associate portal account is issued. Gap: no written checklist for the remote live video examination.
POL-03 Incident Response was approved 2026-09-22 (P06).
The security team and MSSP are trained on the runbooks. Gap: General Counsel, payroll, and communications leads have not trained on their roles.
Planned: executive tabletop of the payroll breach runbook 2026-11-12 and of the payroll outage runbook 2027-02-17 (P08).

The MSSP contains endpoint threats 24x7 and calls the Security Manager within 30 minutes of a high-severity alert. The two P08 runbooks were approved 2026-09-22. Gap: SaaS incidents (payroll, ATS) depend on staff reports because SaaS logs are not monitored.
Incidents are logged in the IT ticketing system under the Security category and tracked to closure.

Notice duties (Florida, other states, E-Verify MOU, MSP clients, insurer) are in the P08 notification matrix. Gap: the MSP 48-hour notice and DHS E-Verify immediate notice were unknown to the incident team before 2026.
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(3)-(4); E-Verify MOU Art. II.A.16

implementation_statement: The MSSP incident response retainer and the insurer panel forensics firm provide response assistance.
The incident response plan is POL-03 with the two P08 runbooks and the notification matrix.
MSSP remote actions use named accounts with MFA. Gap: the timekeeping vendor reaches the fingerprint clocks remotely through a vendor tool with no session approval.

implementation_statement: Paper with SSNs, I-9 copies, and consumer reports goes to locked shred bins with certificates. Laptops are wiped before reuse. Gap: no certificates for 2025 kiosk and clock disposals.
HQ and all branches use badge access with a maintained authorization list; on-site offices are inside client facilities with client badges.
Network closets are locked; paper onboarding files are in locked cabinets. Gap: at 3 branches the network closet is also the supply room and is open during business hours.
The five-policy set and the standards index (P06) were approved 2026-09-22 with an annual review cycle.
This SSP. It also gives the system-level description of the electronic Form I-9 system required by 8 CFR 274a.2(e)(5) (section 10.3).

HR tickets disable SSO access the same day. Gap: E-Verify, VMS, and credentialing client portal accounts are removed by hand and were late in the P07 sample.

The MSSP and integration contractor sign confidentiality terms. Gap: no security requirements or access review for the contractor developers.

implementation_statement: Risk assessment requirements are in POL-01 section 4.
The APATP is categorized Moderate (section 6).
Enterprise risk assessment completed 2026-08-07 with NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01, 52 risks); annual update each July.
Supply chain risks for SaaS vendors are in P01 (R-029 to R-031, R-043). Gap: no tiering or annual vendor reassessment.

The MSSP runs quarterly external and internal authenticated scans. Gap: container images in the integration platform are not scanned, and 9 of 41 critical findings in 2026 H1 exceeded the 30-day target.
Risk responses are recorded in P01 and tracked in the P07 POA&M.
Critical processes and components are identified in the BIA (P05).
The payroll and ATS contracts have security and breach notice terms. Gap: no standard security terms for new vendors; AI vendors were added through the ATS marketplace with click-through terms.

SOC 2 reports are collected for 7 vendors (P09 Part B). Gaps: no tiering; 41 of 64 vendors with personal information have no security terms; the credentialing vendor has no SOC 2 report (EV-042, EV-043, EV-044).
The integration contractor runs unit tests before release. Gap: no security testing or secret scanning of integration code.
The integration code is kept in a hosted repository with pull requests. Gap: no secure development standard in the statement of work.
The career site and APIs are protected by the vendors' denial-of-service services.
Office firewalls and the cloud hub firewall block inbound traffic; workloads have no internet ingress. Gap: kiosks on the staff network at 9 of 14 branches (EV-016).

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: The cloud hub denies by default. Gap: branch firewalls allow all outbound traffic.
TLS 1.2 or higher for all SaaS, the career site, the VMS, and integration APIs; SD-WAN tunnels are encrypted.
Cloud keys are managed in the provider key service with company-managed keys for the warehouse and archive.
Providers use validated cryptographic modules per their SOC 2 system descriptions and service documentation.
SaaS, warehouse, archive, and backup data are encrypted at rest; laptops use full-disk encryption.
Laptop OS and browser patches install automatically. Gap: integration container base images and the fingerprint clocks are not patched on a schedule.
EDR on all laptops and kiosks with 24x7 MSSP response.
The MSSP monitors EDR, IdP, email, firewall, and cloud logs 24x7. Gap: no monitoring of SaaS activity (payroll exports, bank changes, ATS downloads).
The MSSP and the security analyst review vendor advisories and the CISA known exploited vulnerabilities catalog weekly.
The ATS I-9 module locks completed sections. Gap: the scanned I-9 archive has no versioning or object lock and no deletion alert.
Email filtering with external-sender tags and impersonation protection.
The integration platform validates pay rates and required fields before posting to payroll. Gap: time imports from the VMS are not checked for duplicates.

Gap: no enforced retention schedule; I-9s, consumer reports, credential files, and call recordings are kept indefinitely (EV-037). The schedule in POL-04 4.6 takes effect 2026-10-01 with purges starting 2027-01-31.
Planned: remove full SSNs and bank account numbers from the data warehouse (last 4 digits only) by 2026-12-31.
SOC 2 reports are collected but not reviewed systematically; the first 8 structured reviews were done for P09 Part B.
